name: Physics Simulation Validation Protocol
goal: Develop an actionable validation protocol for a research pipeline that reconstructs a real flooded road with 3D Gaussian Splatting, simulates vehicle-water interaction with the Material Point Method, and produces a graded FORD / NO-FORD decision by comparing six-degree-of-freedom vehicle outcomes with civil-engineering flood hazard thresholds. The protocol must be achievable with an existing 36-run parameter sweep, published benchmarks and existing datasets; it should not assume new physical experiments. Search adjacent validation cultures including geotechnical MPM benchmark suites, CFD verification and validation, ASME V&V 20 concepts and Grid Convergence Index practice, robotics and real-to-sim validation, autonomous-vehicle safety-case work, UL 4600 and ISO 21448/SOTIF discussions, and disaster-science forensic validation. Prioritize evidence standards and measurable metrics for four validation layers: component checks, calibration or comparison against trusted reference behavior, sensitivity and numerical-convergence analysis, and held-out stress testing.
summary:
DECISION CREDIBILITY, NOT NUMERICAL AGREEMENT, IS THE GOVERNING ENDPOINT: A FORD CLAIM REQUIRES VALIDATED SIX-DOF OUTCOMES AND A CONSERVATIVE MARGIN TO THE HAZARD THRESHOLD, WHEREAS A NO-FORD CLAIM MAY BE ISSUED WHENEVER UNCERTAINTY SPANS OR EXCEEDS THAT BOUNDARY [Obe04, Eca20, Eas01].

EVIDENCE CHAIN.
- Component verification. Test 3DGS reconstruction against surveyed/known road geometry where available; test MPM separately on analytical flow, dam-break/free-surface, contact, and rigid/elastic-obstacle cases. Report conservation residuals, contact penetration, interface position, pressure/force histories, and convergence, not merely visual plausibility. MPM particle/grid crossing, locking, and stress/pressure oscillation require explicit checks [Bra11, Vau20, Aco19, Coo18]; published dam-break and FSI datasets can substitute for new experiments [Aur23, Sun19c, Zha17].
- Calibration versus validation. Freeze parameters after calibration on a disjoint reference subset; compare held-out trajectories, yaw/roll/pitch, wheel contact/loss, hydrodynamic loads, and threshold-relevant maxima against vehicle-water experiments where available [He26d]. AT EACH VALIDATION POINT REPORT SIGNED DISCREPANCY AND A VALIDATION INTERVAL COMBINING REFERENCE-DATA, NUMERICAL, AND PARAMETER UNCERTAINTY; THIS ESTIMATES MODEL ERROR RATHER THAN PRODUCING A BINARY "VALIDATED" STATUS [Eca20, Col97].
- Numerical and parametric uncertainty. For representative corners and decision-boundary cases, perform at least 3 grid/particle and timestep refinements; report observed order, Richardson/GCI intervals, and iterative residual criteria for every decision quantity [Roa94, Cel07, Ste01]. Propagate depth, velocity, friction/contact, water properties, reconstructed geometry, and model-form alternatives; RETAIN ALEATORY VERSUS EPISTEMIC UNCERTAINTY SEPARATELY [Mul16, Whi19].
- Held-out stress and decision testing. Reserve strata from the sweep, especially threshold-adjacent and extreme cases, BEFORE tuning. Treat the sweep as ODD coverage, not exhaustive proof [Neu20, Wei23, Gyl20]. Issue FORD only when a conservative bound remains within all civil thresholds across the declared ODD; otherwise label NO-FORD or indeterminate, with operational limits and evidence traceability in a UL/SOTIF-style safety argument [Koo23, Put23].
